text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.67% today to $137.86, recovering some ground after a rough two-week slide of 7.51%. The bounce likely reflects a shift in oil market sentiment: crude prices have stabilized after earlier weakness, and Trump's comments on Monday that the Iran conflict would "end fairly soon" have reduced near-term anxiety about supply disruptions. With US oil at $99.64 and Brent at $107.03, the market appears to be pricing in less geopolitical risk than it was a few days ago when crude briefly dipped below $90.

The stock's two-week decline, however, tells a longer story about sector headwinds. Recent midterm election results dealt a blow to fossil fuel interests, with voters rejecting Trump and embracing renewable energy priorities — a structural shift that weighs on oil majors regardless of daily price swings or near-term geopolitical noise.
